data.title: Exxon Mobil Stock (XOM) Climbs on Likely $4.5B Iran War Profit Boost
data.description: Shares in oil giant Exxon Mobil (XOM) edged higher today as it said its Q3 profit is set to be boosted by the ongoing war in the Gulf between the U.S. and Iran. In an SEC filing the company said that higher refining margins during Q3 could boost its downstream profit by $4.5 billion compared with the previous three months. Exxon's stock is already up nearly 50% in the year-to-date as prices surge.
data.author: David Craik

data.title: CoreWeave vs. IREN: One AI Stock to Avoid, One to Embrace, Says Investor
data.description:
CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV) and IREN (NASDAQ:IREN) are both under pressure today, as the market grows jittery about the rising borrowing costs facing AI cloud providers. The pullback adds to recent losses, leaving both stocks down more than 50% over the past year.

The two companies are in the same business. Both rent GPU computing power to AI developers, and both are spending heavily on data centers to keep up with demand. The difference is who pays for the buildout. CoreWeave relies mostly on debt and equity markets, and those markets have turned on the stock in recent weeks. IREN has convinced customers to pay for a large part of its hardware upfront.

That gap is a focal point in recent analyses by an investor using the moniker Infinity Curve (IC), who has been taking a look at both stocks. The investor keeps coming back to one question: once the chips are bought and the lenders are paid, how much is actually left for shareholders?

Promotion

Double your CRWV exposure with Tradr's CWVX

With CoreWeave, IC's concern starts with the bond market. CRWV shares have been hammered over the past week, while the company's five-year credit default swaps moved past 1,000 basis points, and its unsecured notes due 2031 fell far enough to yield close to 15%. IC notes that none of this means the company has missed a payment or broken a covenant. But for a business that depends on outside money to grow, a sharp jump in funding costs is hard to wave away.

The balance sheet shows why. At the end of June, CoreWeave carried about $35.6 billion in debt principal and $16.3 billion in operating lease liabilities, compared with $5.5 billion in unrestricted cash. Its free cash flow deficit grew from roughly $4.7 billion in Q1 to $5.7 billion in Q2.

The two pressures also reinforce each other. A September agreement lets CoreWeave sell up to 35 million shares. At the October 7 price, that block was worth about $3.1 billion. After the selloff, it was worth roughly $2.4 billion. Expensive debt makes selling stock more attractive, but a lower stock price means more dilution for every dollar raised.

On the other hand, the investor doesn't see a demand problem. Nothing suggests customers are walking away, and the company guided Q3 revenue to $3.45 billion to $3.60 billion. What matters to IC is whether new capacity brings in more cash on its own, rather than needing more corporate debt or new shares to fund it.

At around 1.6x consensus 2027 sales, the stock looks cheap for a company expected to more than double revenue. The investor argues, though, that a sales multiple ignores debt, leases, and the cost of replacing GPUs. As such, IC takes a bearish view here now. "I sold my CRWV shares a few days ago, and for now, I am staying on the sidelines until I see clearer confirmation that financing conditions are stabilizing," IC summed up, rating the stock a Sell. (To watch Infinity Curve's track record, click here)

IREN looks different to the investor because of how its assets age. GPUs need replacing every few years, but power connections, cooling systems and buildings can serve several generations of chips. Recent IREN customers have prepaid 45% to 55% of GPU costs, and lenders have covered up to about 90% of GPU spending on some deployments. With contracts bringing in more than $20 million per megawatt each year, management estimates the GPUs can pay for themselves in about two years. In effect, the first customer helps pay for infrastructure that will outlast its contract.

That's where IC sees the real upside. The next deployment starts with a site that's already partly paid for, so most new spending goes to chips rather than rebuilding everything. Each successful contract leaves IREN in a stronger position for the next one, and over time that could push returns well above what today's financial statements show. Management also says older GPUs can keep earning after their five-year depreciation period by moving from AI training to simpler inference work, which would improve the economics further.

The investor's main caveat is about cash. Most of IREN's operating cash flow in the June quarter came from customer prepayments for services not yet delivered, and collecting cash early isn't the same as generating free cash. The figure to watch is cash per megawatt after debt payments, maintenance and reserves.

On valuation, IREN trades at 5.64x forward EV/sales, below peers MARA at 8.30x and RIOT at 9.97x, two bitcoin miners also moving into AI infrastructure. Its expected revenue growth of about 143% is the highest in that group. It also trades at 8.43x forward EBITDA, with EBITDA growth projected at around 178%. With $4 billion in contracted annual revenue and plenty of capacity still to develop, IC thinks the market hasn't caught up to the AI buildout. "I continue to be bullish on IREN as the upside story goes beyond the first GPU cycle," IC wrapped up. "If the cost of computing is recovered by the customers in their funded deployments while the renewable energy and data center structure is left behind, profits will continue to get better with each cycle."

As such, Infinity Curve rates IREN stock a Buy.

On the Street, both stocks receive Moderate Buy consensus ratings and are projected to generate big gains. CRWV's $143.59 average price target points to 12-month returns of 126%. Meanwhile, IREN is expected to gain an even more impressive 183%, given the average target lands at $79.30. (See CRWV stock forecast or IREN stock forecast)

data.title: Google (GOOGL) Secures Access to CNN News Content for AI Training
data.description:
Google parent company Alphabet (GOOGL) has secured access to the news content of broadcaster CNN, which it will use to train artificial intelligence (AI) models and agents. CNN said it is joining forces with Alphabet and will use the technology company's AI capabilities to enhance its viewer engagement.

At the same time, Google gains access to CNN's content for AI-generated purposes and online responses in its search engine. However, CNN has not outlined how it will incorporate AI to drive audiences towards its content, which is mostly comprised of videos and television news reports. For Alphabet, the deal is more clear as it will provide additional content on which the company can train AI models.
data.author: Joel Baglole

data.title: Interactive Brokers (IBKR) Raises Dividend 71%
data.description:
Interactive Brokers (IBKR) has increased its quarterly dividend payment by 71%. The U.S. brokerage and stock trading platform has lifted its distribution to shareholders to $0.15 per share each quarter from $0.0875 previously. The new dividend amount will lift the yield on IBKR stock closer to 1% from 0.41% currently.

The new dividend is scheduled to be paid on Dec. 14 of this year to shareholders of record as of Dec. 1. This is the second consecutive year that the company has raised its distribution. Interactive Brokers had maintained a modest quarterly dividend payout of $0.025 for several years. Since the end of 2024, the company has raised its quarterly dividend by 500%.

data.title: Apple Stock (AAPL) Rises as iPhone Duo Sells Out in Minutes, Deliveries Pushed to January
data.description:
Shares of tech giant Apple (AAPL) are up at the time of writing after pre-orders for its $1,999 iPhone Duo sold out within minutes. According to Bloomberg, the company's first foldable iPhone became difficult to secure almost immediately after pre-orders opened at 8 a.m. Eastern. As a result, Apple's online store showed January delivery estimates for both colors and every storage configuration.

The iPhone Duo officially launches on October 23, although customers who missed the initial inventory may now have to wait for more than three months.

The device features a 5.4-inch outer display that opens into a 7.6-inch screen, which allows users to switch between a conventional smartphone and a small tablet. The strong initial response comes as Apple enters a market that Samsung (SSNLF) has served for years with its Galaxy Z Fold smartphones. However, the shipping delays don't necessarily mean that Apple received an unusually large number of orders.

Promotion

Want cash flow from the tech industry without leaving it? Meet TDAQ.

This is because the company hasn't disclosed how many units were available when pre-orders opened. Supply could also explain the shortages. In fact, a September report suggested that only slightly more than 60% of assembled iPhone Duo units were meeting manufacturing requirements at that time, though Apple hasn't confirmed that figure.

Could the iPhone Duo Generate Billions in New Revenue?

Research firm Counterpoint expects Apple to sell approximately 6 million iPhone Duos before the end of 2026. At the $1,999 starting price, that would represent roughly $12 billion in potential sales. However, Apple's ability to reach that forecast depends partly on how quickly it can manufacture additional devices.

Meanwhile, Apple's existing iPhone business remains strong. Revenue from iPhones grew by 22% to $54.25 billion in the June quarter, while total company revenue increased by 16% to $109.4 billion.

Is Apple a Buy or Sell Right Now?

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Moderate Buy consensus rating on AAPL stock based on 16 Buys, 11 Holds, and four Sells assigned in the past three months, as indicated by the graphic below. Furthermore, the average AAPL price target of $334.91 per share implies that shares are trading near fair value. (See AAPL's Stock Forecast).

data.title: 'A Nothingburger,' Says Investor About Rocket Lab Stock
data.description:
Rocket Lab (NASDAQ:RKLB) investors really did not appreciate the space company's latest update and headed to the exit gate in droves on Thursday, after the company said the first flight of its Neutron rocket will slip into 2027 and miss its earlier fourth-quarter 2026 target.

Neutron forms a big part of the Rocket Lab bull case because it can carry far heavier payloads than the company's smaller Electron rocket, which would let Rocket Lab pursue larger commercial and government missions and compete more directly with SpaceX. Investors had been counting on a year-end launch to lift the stock, after it had already endured a massive pullback from May's high.

But as any savvy investor knows, the market sometimes has a tendency to overreact to bad news, and in this case, investor Amrita Roy believes that is the case. In fact, Roy calls the selloff a gift, as she thinks the market is overlooking the bigger picture.

CEO Peter Beck explained that inspectors found voids, which are tiny air pockets, between the carbon fiber layers of a forward propellant tank dome on the rocket's first stage. These gaps can weaken the part. This is Neutron's second manufacturing setback, following an earlier tank issue that pushed Rocket Lab toward automated production.

Rocket Lab hasn't set a new launch date yet. Beck said the replacement dome should be built and inspected before the first quarter of 2027, with tank assembly and testing during that quarter, and only then will the company name a target. Engineers were able to recreate the defect and adjust the process, which Roy sees as a sign of a fixable production issue rather than a deeper engineering problem. Rocket Lab is also using the extra time to bring forward upgrades meant for later flights, with the second and third rockets already in production. Beck also expects more Neutron contracts to be announced.

Meanwhile, the rest of the company is doing well. Second-quarter revenue reached a record $234.1 million, up 62% year-over-year, while the backlog hit about $2.36 billion, with nearly half expected to turn into revenue within a year. Since Space Systems brings in over 80% of sales, Roy sees a solid cushion while Neutron catches up.

The upcoming Iridium deal adds to the appeal. Iridium shareholders approved the acquisition in September, and once regulators sign off, Rocket Lab will gain a 66-satellite constellation and valuable L-band spectrum. Roy believes this brings the company closer to controlling everything from building satellites to selling services, a model only SpaceX has so far.

All of that makes RKLB a Buy to Roy, although the investor is only making it a small position, given the "volatile nature of the company." (To watch Roy's track record, click here)

Most of the Street's analysts also see the stock as a sound choice. Based on 15 Buys vs. 3 Holds, the analyst consensus rates the stock a Strong Buy. Meanwhile, the $100.25 average price target points to 12-month returns of 87%. (See RKLB stock forecast)

data.title: S&P 500 Slips as Tech Stocks Remain Under Pressure
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SPX) is down 0.07% on Friday as tech stocks continue to sell off, highlighted by losses in AMD (AMD), Micron (MU), and Dell (DELL). Software stocks, which rallied on Thursday, are facing pressure as well, with cybersecurity stocks particularly weak.

In recent days, investor concern has intensified over tech valuations, heavy investments in data centers, and circular financing deals between AI companies and chipmakers. These concerns have weighed on tech stocks as investors question whether the massive spending on AI and data centers will pay off. Outside of tech, most of the other S&P 500 sectors are trading higher on the day, including energy, financial, and consumer defensive.

Warsh Comments Weigh on Rate Hike Expectations

Meanwhile, rate hike expectations are trending lower after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh spoke at an International Monetary Fund (IMF) event in Bangkok, Thailand on Thursday evening. While Warsh declined to signal the Fed's next move, investors viewed his approach as dovish. "I don't prejudge meetings," he said. "I don't believe in saying now what I might do at the meetings that we have in the balance of this year."

data.title: Tesla Stock Gains on Flying Roadster Demo, but Gene Munster Sees 'No Commercial Value'
data.description:
Tesla (TSLA) stock opened 1% higher at Friday's market open after the company revealed its next-generation Roadster. The electric sports car uses SpaceX (SPCX)-designed thrusters to perform aerial maneuvers. Deepwater Asset Management Managing Partner Gene Munster called the reveal an "engineering flex" but said it offers "no commercial value beyond embarrassing traditional carmakers."

Munster Sees Tesla and SpaceX Moving Closer Together

Munster is a longtime tech analyst who spent more than 20 years at Piper Jaffray before co-founding Deepwater Asset Management. He said the event showed how Elon Musk could bring Tesla and SpaceX closer together. In a post on X, Munster described the Roadster as a "mashup of the two tech teams." He added, "Elon can't wait" to bring the companies together.

Dan Ives, an analyst at Yorkville Ives and a longtime Tesla bull, shared a similar view. He stated the Roadster reveal showed where Tesla and SpaceX's engineering efforts could go together. Ives called the car's SpaceX-developed hardware "a small example of the synergies between Tesla and SpaceX."

Promotion

Two ETFs for long or short leverage on SPCX

The merger speculation followed a note from Barclays analyst Dan Levy earlier this week. He said a Tesla-SpaceX deal could be announced before Tesla's annual shareholder meeting in December. Levy suggested SpaceX could acquire Tesla in an all-stock deal, with Tesla shareholders receiving SpaceX shares instead of cash.

Other Experts Weigh In

Future Fund Managing Partner Gary Black said the Roadster is impressive from a tech standpoint but is unlikely to add much to Tesla's earnings. If Tesla sells 3,000 Roadsters a year and earns $100,000 per car, the model would add about $0.06 per share to the company's projected 2029 earnings of $5.40 per share.

Black remains cautious on Tesla due to its high valuation and lower earnings estimates for 2027–2030.

Meanwhile, Angel investor Jason Calacanis said in a post on X that videos of the flying Roadster looked like "science fiction," even though they were real. He seemed impressed by the demo and asked what might be possible if the car could stay in the air for five minutes, 10 minutes, or even 30 minutes.

Is TSLA Stock a Buy?

Tesla is set to report its third-quarter 2026 results on October 21. Wall Street expects adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $0.45, down from $0.50 a year earlier. Revenue is forecast to dip slightly to $27.94 billion.

Tesla stock has a consensus Moderate Buy rating based on 14 Buys, 11 Holds, and two Sells issued in the last three months. The average TSLA price target of $404.87 implies 10.10% upside from current levels.
